clue.text: Swine finally settled on camp whiskers

indicators.note: in a charade, on means the following pieces come after the first one

parts.note: a camp is a faction or party, one side in a dispute
a boar is a male pig, a swine

indicators.note: finally picks out the last letter of the word settled

explanation.surface: A pig has at last come to rest on the campsite, with a hint of whiskers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes the last letter of 'settled'; 'on' puts the pig and that letter after the camp. Sideboards is a mainly British term for sideburns.
explanation.definitionFit: Sideboards is a British word for sideburns, the strips of hair grown down the cheeks, so a kind of whiskers.

clue.text: Left gongs round danglers?

parts.note: gongs is British slang for medals or honours, such as the OBE (Order of the British Empire)

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned medals arranged around things that hang down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gongs' looks like percussion, but in British slang it means honours such as the OBE (Officer of the Order of the British Empire).
explanation.definitionFit: Earlobes are the rounded fleshy parts that hang at the bottom of the ears, playfully called round danglers.

clue.text: Excited rescuers here for series of updates?

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters of the following words are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Thrilled lifeboat crews have turned up for a run of news bulletins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excited' scrambles RESCUERS HERE FOR into the answer. The question mark warns that the definition is playful: a training course updates your skills.
explanation.definitionFit: A short training course that brings someone's knowledge up to date amounts to a set of updates on their skills.

clue.text: Writer starts to chew it languidly

definitions.text: Writer starts to chew it languidly

parts.note: a pen is an instrument for writing, a writer

indicators.note: starts to picks out the opening letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: An author begins nibbling at something lazily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts to' gives CIL from 'chew it languidly'. Read whole, the clue also describes the item: a writing tool you might gnaw idly while thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: A pencil is a writing implement, and one is famously chewed at the end by a dawdling writer.

clue.text: Suave fellow endlessly threw around subject to debate

indicators.note: around means the shortened word is wrapped about the next piece
endlessly removes the final letter of the word

parts.note: to shy something is to throw it, so threw gives shied
a moot point is one open to argument

explanation.surface: A slick man keeps tossing a debatable topic about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the final D; 'around' wraps the shortened throw about the debatable word.
explanation.definitionFit: A smoothie is a charming, polished, sometimes ingratiating man, a smooth operator.

clue.text: Bury conviction relating to diversity of thought

parts.note: to inter is to bury a body
faith is a firm belief, a conviction

explanation.surface: Suppress a strong belief about variety of opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: Interfaith describes relations between different religions, a matter of differing beliefs and thought.

clue.text: Waffle about old sweet

indicators.note: about means the word is turned round

parts.note: to gas is to talk idly, to waffle

explanation.surface: Rambling talk about an old-fashioned pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the waffle word round; 'Waffle' looks like a breakfast item but is idle talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Sago pudding is a traditional British dessert, so sago here stands for a sweet course.

clue.text: Bogus son acting without subtlety

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son in family trees
ham acting is overdone, unsubtle performing

explanation.surface: A fake boy overacts on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Sham as an adjective means fake or counterfeit, a synonym of bogus.

clue.text: Ten in front of ship? Adequate enough, say

parts.note: the fore is the forward part of a ship
X is the Roman numeral for ten
ample means more than sufficient

explanation.surface: A ten at the prow of a vessel is quite enough, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link here, joining the ten to the ship's front before the adequate word.
explanation.definitionFit: Say is used to introduce an instance, exactly as the phrase for instance is.

clue.text: Face off the best judge being knowledgeable

indicators.note: face off means the front letter is removed

parts.note: the elite are the best of a group
to rate is to assess or judge

explanation.surface: A face-off between the top performers and a judge who knows it all.
explanation.definitionFit: Literate means well read or educated in a subject, which is to be knowledgeable.

clue.text: Joker, singular, the very best

parts.note: S is the grammar abbreviation for singular
the cream is the finest part of anything

explanation.surface: A comedian who is unique and top of the class.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a scream means they are hilarious, a real comic or joker.

clue.text: Support advertiser's possibly irresponsible advisors

parts.note: to back is to support

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Endorse an ad man's dubious consultants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' scrambles ADVERTISERS, the 's counting as its S, into SEATDRIVERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Back-seat drivers give unwanted, unaccountable instructions, so they are advisers who bear no responsibility.

clue.text: Do time, calm at first

indicators.note: at first puts the calm word ahead of the time letter

parts.note: even means level and calm, as of temper

explanation.surface: Serve a sentence, staying placid to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' looks like a verb but is the noun: a party or function.
explanation.definitionFit: A do is an informal word for a party or social occasion, an event.

clue.text: Stirring maiden ton gets put up

indicators.note: stirring mixes things up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rousing first-innings century wins a player selection.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden ton is a cricketer's first century, a hundred runs, and 'Stirring' scrambles those words.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone up for a post or award is to propose them as a candidate.

clue.text: Axe: that is to say, strike

parts.note: SC abbreviates scilicet, Latin for namely or that is to say
to rap is to strike sharply

explanation.surface: Chop down, which is to say hit.
explanation.definitionFit: To axe a plan is to cancel or abandon it, which is to scrap it.

clue.text: The real thing, perhaps

parts.note: definite means certain, real rather than imagined
an article is an object, a thing

explanation.surface: The genuine object, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the first word 'The'; 'perhaps' marks it as one example of the category.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar, the word 'the' is the English example of this part of speech.

clue.text: Very good part of speech lifted lines for priest's book

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted means the letters are read upward, i.e. reversed

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written here as AI
a verb is one of the parts of speech
RY is short for railway, railway lines

explanation.surface: Fine bits of a sermon raised along with lines from a cleric's prayer book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' turns AI and VERB together into BREVIA, then RY completes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A breviary is the book containing the daily services that Catholic priests recite.

clue.text: Pine store with opening put off

indicators.note: the opening letter is put off, that is removed

parts.note: a cache is a hidden store

explanation.surface: A shop delays its launch amid yearning.
explanation.definitionFit: To pine for something is to long for it, as to ache for it.

clue.text: Mysterious and duller substance?

parts.note: dark can mean obscure or mysterious
matter is the comparative of matt, meaning less shiny or duller

explanation.surface: An enigmatic and drabber material.
explanation.walkthrough: MATTER is read as 'more matt', a less glossy finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Dark matter is the unseen material thought to make up much of the universe's mass, a substance.

clue.text: Chump fences fine watch

indicators.note: fences means encloses, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a loon is a fool, a chump
OK means fine or all right

explanation.surface: An idiot puts up railings round a good timepiece.
explanation.definitionFit: To look on is to watch as a spectator without taking part.

clue.text: Do hard by it — quietly take exception to gift

indicators.note: to do something over is to rework it, so these words are reworked into a new order

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
to resent is to take offence at

explanation.surface: Be tough about it, then silently object to a present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' scrambles HARD BY IT into BIRTHDAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A present given on someone's anniversary of being born is a kind of gift.

clue.text: One in the dock rising to undermine checks

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the letters read upward, so both words are reversed

parts.note: to erode is to wear away, to undermine
vets means examines or checks

explanation.surface: A defendant getting up to sabotage inspections.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One in the dock' suggests a defendant, but it is a docker. 'rising' turns ERODE and VETS together into STEVEDORE.
explanation.definitionFit: A stevedore is a docker who loads and unloads ships, so works in a dock.

clue.text: Put out warning to a convoy

indicators.note: put out means disturbed, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Issue a caution to a line of vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: A wagon train is a line of wagons travelling together, as pioneers did, so a convoy.

clue.text: In Spanish sun oil's left to sink: not able to be cleared up

definitions.text: not able to be cleared up

parts.note: sol is the Spanish for sun

indicators.note: to sink means the letter moves down, in a down clue to the bottom of the word

parts.note: lube, short for lubricant, is oil

explanation.surface: Suntan oil dumped in Spain sinks without dissolving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to sink' moves L of LUBE to its foot, giving UBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: An insoluble problem cannot be solved, so cannot be cleared up.

clue.text: Reform contains permission

indicators.note: to reform is to reshape, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A reform package includes approval.
explanation.definitionFit: A sanction can mean official approval or authorisation, i.e. permission.

clue.text: Cheers for place

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
to sit something is to place it

explanation.surface: A toast in favour of a location.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosit is a German and Latin drinking toast, used like cheers.

clue.text: Pondered on American being in sea

indicators.note: being in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: Thought about a Yank afloat in the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: To muse is to think deeply, a synonym of ponder.

clue.text: A mother's the first of us, some would say

definitions.text: the first of us, some would say

parts.note: a dam is a mother, especially of an animal

explanation.surface: A mother is the origin of humanity, in some opinions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some would say' makes the definition fair: in the Bible, believers hold him to be the first human.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis he is the first man created, the forefather of humankind.
